project.title: PRAIN — Semantic Control Plane for Autonomous Agents
project.purpose: Independent, evidence-aware semantic control plane for autonomous agents: observations, claims, goals, policy-checked actions, verified outcomes, identity continuity, and adaptive coordination across the five P/R/A/I/N dimensions. PRAIN is not dependent on Hallerbans; Hallerbans is one possible consumer.
project.status: Canonical content baseline v0.3.0; 20 claims individually source-mapped and reviewed on 2026-10-20. Scope-specific and design-synthesis claims remain explicitly qualified.

dimensions.name: R — Reason / Denken & Gedächtnis
dimensions.summary: Reason (R) interprets and compares evidence, builds hypotheses, retrieves relevant memory and plans; derived claims must link premises and method/version. Memory storage itself is cross-cutting.

claims.claim: A three-layer memory model is a useful architecture pattern.
claims.status: Supported as a design pattern; not a universal industry standard.
claims.assessment_note: The three-layer pattern is a design synthesis across memory products/projects, not a universal industry standard or a direct proposition established by one source.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: Mem0 universally saves more than 90% of tokens.
claims.status: Not established as a universal result; requires the specific benchmark and comparison setup.
claims.assessment_note: The primary paper reports >90% token-cost savings in a specified LOCOMO/full-context comparison. “Universally” is unsupported; preserve the benchmark and baseline scope.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: A-Mem's core method is GRPO-based memory routing.
claims.status: Mischaracterizes the cited A-Mem paper; its central approach is dynamic, Zettelkasten-inspired memory organization.
claims.assessment_note: The cited A-MEM primary paper describes dynamically organized, Zettelkasten-inspired linked memories; it does not establish GRPO-based memory routing as A-MEM's core method. Do not conflate it with the separate steering/GRPO paper S13.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: Memory benchmarks show that recall alone does not guarantee success in multi-step tasks.
claims.status: Broadly supported; exact percentages depend on benchmark, model and setup.
claims.assessment_note: The survey covers memory mechanisms and evaluation challenges; the general caution is reasonable, but task success depends on benchmark/model/agent loop and the entry should not be read as a universal quantitative result.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

dimensions.implementation_notes: Keep current task state, durable project facts and execution history distinct. Evaluate memory systems against real multi-step tasks instead of selecting by benchmark headline alone.

dimensions.name: N — Nerve / Ausführung & Handeln
dimensions.summary: Nerve (N) is the capability-mediated execution surface that performs only policy-authorized actions, emits receipts, and supplies verifiable evidence. Runtime/OS implementations are replaceable infrastructure.

claims.claim: AIOS is a real research architecture for managing LLM-agent resources.
claims.status: Supported.
claims.assessment_note: Repository and primary paper establish AIOS as a research architecture for LLM-agent resources. This verifies existence/scope, not adoption or production maturity.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: AIOS is the universally adopted primary agent OS standard.
claims.status: Overstated; no such universal standard is established.
claims.assessment_note: No evidence checked establishes universal adoption or a single universally adopted agent-OS standard. The cited project is one research architecture.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: AIOS can yield up to 2.1× speed-up.
claims.status: A reported result under particular experiments, not a general guarantee.
claims.assessment_note: The up-to-2.1× figure appears in the paper for particular experiments. Preserve “up to”, baseline, task and implementation context; do not promote it to a universal performance estimate.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: Cloud runtimes guarantee memory access under 100 ms.
claims.status: Not substantiated as a universal guarantee by the listed documentation.
claims.assessment_note: Checked official vendor documentation does not establish a universal <100 ms memory-access guarantee. Cloud/runtime guarantees are product-, path-, region-, load- and configuration-specific.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

dimensions.implementation_notes: Prioritize a reliable Linux runtime, persistent task state, restart/resume, timeouts, concurrency limits, observability and controlled hand-offs before adopting a full research Agent OS.

dimensions.name: P — Perception / Sinne & Beobachtung
dimensions.summary: Perception (P) normalizes observations from sensors, tools, user reports and external sources; it preserves provenance, uncertainty, scope and timestamps. Observation is not the same as truth.

claims.claim: MCP standardizes connections to tools and data sources.
claims.status: Supported; it standardizes interfaces, not correctness or authorization by itself.
claims.assessment_note: The official MCP specification describes standardized protocol interfaces for client/server interaction with tools and resources. Verification is limited to this scope; MCP itself does not certify the called tool as safe.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: Poorly written tool descriptions can impair tool selection and waste context.
claims.status: Supported as an active research concern; quantitative benefits need specific evidence.
claims.assessment_note: The primary 2026 study empirically examined 856 tools across 103 servers and found description-quality problems with measurable but mixed outcome effects. Keep the model/task/sample scope and trade-offs.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: MCP is a universal, fully secure industry standard.
claims.status: Overstated; security depends on implementation, permissions and deployment.
claims.assessment_note: Neither a protocol specification nor general security guidance supports the claim that MCP is universally and fully secure. Security depends on implementation, authorization, tool permissions and deployment.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: Event-triggered perception is a useful architecture pattern.
claims.status: Plausible and established as a general systems pattern, not unique to 2026.
claims.assessment_note: Architecture synthesis only: event-triggered perception is a common systems pattern. No specific external empirical source is asserted for this general design statement.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

dimensions.implementation_notes: Maintain a small, clear tool catalog. Specify purpose, input/output schema, limits and failure modes; verify effects from observed system state rather than trusting the model's narration.

dimensions.name: I — Intention / Ziele & Wille
dimensions.summary: Intention (I) represents goals, priorities, dependencies, constraints and measurable acceptance criteria. It proposes plans; it cannot grant execution permissions.

claims.claim: LLM agents can drift from original goals during long tasks.
claims.status: Supported by research; severity varies by model and task.
claims.assessment_note: Research supports goal drift as a studied failure mode in extended agent tasks; severity depends on task, model and scaffold.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: Goal drift inevitably begins after 100,000 tokens.
claims.status: Not supported as a universal threshold.
claims.assessment_note: The cited study does not establish inevitable onset after 100,000 tokens; it reports nearly perfect adherence by its best-performing scaffolded model beyond 100,000 tokens in its hardest setting while still finding some drift across evaluated models.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: A steering agent can reduce goal drift.
claims.status: Promising research direction; effectiveness is task- and setup-dependent.
claims.assessment_note: The 2026 preprint reports a steering agent improving performance/efficiency in information-seeking tasks. This is emerging research, not a universal or production-validated guarantee.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: Goal drift can be driven nearly to zero by the described binding/commitment split.
claims.status: Not established by the cited evidence.
claims.assessment_note: The checked sources do not establish that a binding/commitment split drives goal drift nearly to zero. No quantitative promise should be repeated without a named evaluation and baseline.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

dimensions.implementation_notes: Store the goal and measurable acceptance criteria outside the transient model context. Check each major step against them; mark work complete only when the result is independently verified.

dimensions.name: A — Anima / Selbstmodell & Kontinuität
dimensions.summary: Anima (A) is the explicit, inspectable, versioned self-model and continuity record. It is not a claim of consciousness and is not the policy authorization authority.

claims.claim: Agent systems benefit from identity, scoped authorization and auditability.
claims.status: Strong architecture principle; exact implementations vary.
claims.assessment_note: Identity, scoped authorization and auditability are architectural control principles supported by the risk and trust standards landscape; exact mechanisms and assurance levels vary.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: ERC-8004 replaces local identity and access management.
claims.status: Incorrect; agent discovery/trust mechanisms do not replace local authorization controls.
claims.assessment_note: ERC-8004 is an agent discovery/trust-related standard proposal; it does not replace application-local authentication, authorization, tenant isolation or policy enforcement.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: x402 and AP2 are real protocol initiatives for agent-related payments.
claims.status: Supported; adoption and maturity should not be overstated.
claims.assessment_note: Official x402 and AP2 project records establish these as real payment/protocol initiatives. This is not a claim of universal adoption, maturity or safety.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

claims.claim: TEEs automatically make an autonomous agent trustworthy.
claims.status: Incorrect; TEEs address specific isolation/integrity properties, not the full trust problem.
claims.assessment_note: A trusted execution environment can provide bounded isolation/attestation properties; it does not by itself make the whole agent, its inputs, tools, policies or external effects trustworthy.
claims.confidence_method: legacy qualitative editor assessment; not a calibrated probability

dimensions.implementation_notes: Give the agent a clear service identity, scoped credentials and auditable action logs. Treat crypto identity and autonomous payments as optional capabilities, not prerequisites for general autonomy.

cross_cutting.name: Security across all dimensions
cross_cutting.summary: Security is enforced across all dimensions by explicit policy, scoped principal/tenant boundaries, capability checks, human approval where required, evidence/audit, revocation, and least authority; no P/R/A/I/N dimension is itself a universal authorization bypass.

cross_cutting.name: Evidence quality & claim verification
cross_cutting.summary: Claims carry provenance and evidence; source quality, capture time, scope, transformations, counterevidence, integrity checks and verification procedures are tracked independently from confidence.

cross_cutting.name: Evaluation & feedback loops
cross_cutting.summary: Measure task success, recovery, tool correctness, memory usefulness, cost, latency and goal adherence on representative tasks.

relations.label: R provides interpretations and candidate plans; I owns explicit goal contracts and priorities.
Intention proposes commands; only the independent policy gateway authorizes, and N executes after authorization.
Runtime makes tools and sensors available
A supplies identity/self-model context and declared limits; it never independently grants execution permission.
A may supply identity context to governance; security policy remains cross-cutting and is enforced by the policy gateway.
N emits execution receipts and observed outcomes; authoritative storage/commit rules determine which state becomes durable.
I/R may incorporate only outcome evidence that has been checked under the applicable verification policy.
Observations may alter goal feasibility, but a goal change must be recorded as a revision with an attributable decision.

priority.item: Persistent task state and verifiable completion criteria
priority.why: Makes long-running work resumable and separates activity from success.

priority.item: Tool catalog with clear schemas and post-action verification
priority.why: Reduces ambiguous tool use and unverified claims of success.

priority.item: Layered memory with explicit project facts and execution history
priority.why: Supports continuity without putting everything into one undifferentiated memory store.
Makes actions attributable and limits unnecessary authority.
Measures actual improvement before adding more frameworks or agents.

priority.item: Add a temporal graph or learned steering agent only if tests show need
priority.why: Advanced components should solve measured gaps rather than add complexity by default.
Optional until autonomous paid API use or cross-organization agent commerce is a real requirement.

metadata.html_policy: HTML is a rendered view; database payload must match this file exactly after JSON parsing
metadata.review_note: Source claims are not automatically verified by inclusion in the knowledge base.
metadata.source_review_scope: Primary/official pages were inspected for identity and claim scope; not a systematic review, peer-review assessment or independent experiment replication.
metadata.confidence_note: Legacy qualitative High/Medium/Low labels are retained for historical continuity and must not be treated as numeric probabilities.
